title: Trace overhead throttle with deferred exemplarization and tail-preserving sampling
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Recent perf regression analysis showed ~8-12% CPU and tail-latency increase on RPC hotpaths caused by expensive exemplar extraction and span-metadata formatting in the tracing hot path. Goal: reduce hot-path CPU allocations and p99 latency from tracing without losing visibility into important tail events. Approach: introduce an adaptive, multi-stage mitigation called 'deferred exemplarization' plus a small tail-preserving reservoir sampler and per-tenant throttle. This ticket covers the runtime changes, a config/flag surface, and the rollout plan.
non_goals: We are not changing sampling policy semantics for existing stored traces (no data migration), and not moving to a fully out-of-band trace ingest pipeline in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath CPU attributable to tracing decreases by >=60% in microbench (allocations and wall CPU)
p99 request latency across high-QPS services improves by >=5ms in canary region under synthetic load
Tail-preserving reservoir retains >=95% of latency outliers compared to current baseline (measured with shadow replay)
Feature flag exists with three rollout stages: off, defer-only, defer+reservoir; can be toggled per-tenant via runtime config
Automated dashboards updated: trace-rt-overhead, exemplar-drop-rate, reservoir-hit-rate, per-tenant-throttle-events
design_summary: 1) On hot path, replace immediate exemplar construction with a lightweight tokenized hint (exemplar-hash + minimal metadata) and fast early-exit heuristics. 2) Emit a sparse placeholder to the trace emitter and enqueue a deferred exemplar job (small, bounded work) to a background worker for candidate traces. 3) Implement a tiny reservoir sampler keyed by (service, route) that preserves tail events: when a trace exceeds latency/error thresholds, the deferred worker attempts to attach a full exemplar and mark the trace for full retention. 4) Add per-tenant leaky-bucket throttle to bound background work during storms. 5) Instrument control signals and add feature flag for staged rollout.
implementation_tasks: hotpath: replace exemplar assembly with exemplar-hash + flags (C++/Go depending on service)
background worker: new deferred-exemplar processor with idempotent attach semantics
reservoir: implement tiny in-process reservoir (bounded memory) and periodic eviction policy
throttling: per-tenant leaky-bucket implementation and metrics
flags/config: runtime config and per-tenant toggles in control plane
tests: microbench for CPU/allocations, e2e synthetic traffic replay for tail fidelity
dashboards/alerts: SLOs and new panels to track exemplar attach latency and drop rates
docs: runbook and rollout playbook for Canary -> Gradual -> Global
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Deferred worker backlog could grow during incidents -> Mitigation: per-tenant throttle + backpressure signal to ingress to temporarily reduce sampling rate
Risk: Deferred attach race with trace lifecycle -> Mitigation: idempotent attach and short-lived retention window extended for candidate traces
Risk: Reservoir bias leading to missed classes of outliers -> Mitigation: keep small telemetry shadow (1%) with full immediate exemplars for comparison during rollout
Risk: Operational complexity -> Mitigation: implement concise dashboards and an automated kill-switch that disables deferred processing if worker queue > threshold
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): unit tests + microbenching in local CI
Stage 1 (canary): enable defer-only flag for 5 low-traffic services in prod region-1 for 72h; monitor CPU and p99
Stage 2 (gradual): enable reservoir+defer for 10% of tenants, keep 1% shadow baseline with full immediate exemplars
Stage 3 (global): enable by default with per-tenant opt-out and throttles active
Rollback: feature flag off + drain deferred queue; if queue can't be drained, disable sampling at ingress for affected tenants
